- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 3–8% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is falling, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to avoid underreaction.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast deviates >10% from recent 5-day average, revert toward that average in next 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility amplification.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast with sentiment trend only if sentiment >0.35 for 3+ consecutive days.
